subject: Recap + Next Steps: Context-length profiling & token-volume for pricing
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T15:02:00Z
Subject: Recap + Next Steps: Context-length profiling & token-volume for pricing

Hi Samir / Claire —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and a few asks so we can size pricing for Acme:

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use case: customer support assistant + multi-doc search-based summarization for enterprise docs.
- Expected QPS: bursty during business hours; today ~200 requests/day, target growth to ~5k requests/day in 12 months.
- Current rough monthly token estimate: 500M prompt tokens / 1.2B completion tokens (total ~1.7B tokens) — we'd like you to confirm.

Specific info we need to finalize a pricing recommendation (ideally by EOD Thurs):
1) Typical per-request token breakdown (avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens). Please share percentiles if available (p50/p90).
2) Percent of requests requiring extended context beyond 8k (approx split across 8k / 32k / 128k).
3) Target monthly budget range ($) or target $/1M tokens you want us to aim for (if you have internal benchmarks).
4) Any constraints on model family (open models acceptable?) or latency SLOs (p95 token-latency target).

Attached: Redwood_pricing_sheet_v3.pdf (draft unit economics by model family) and ContextLength_Profile_Template.xlsx — fill the template with a representative sample of 100 requests if possible and return.

Next steps
- If you confirm the numbers above, we’ll run a short cost-sensitivity model and propose 2 pricing options: (A) Balanced: lower latency with moderate cost, (B) Cost-optimized: batching + quantized models and tighter caching.
- We can run a short 1-week pilot on Dedicated with a pricing cap if you want to validate unit economics.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Jordan to scope the profiling exercise and a proposed timeline.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

---
Attachment: Redwood_pricing_sheet_v3.pdf (pdf, 120KB stub)
Attachment: ContextLength_Profile_Template.xlsx (xlsx, 30KB stub)

From: Samir Patel <samir@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Liu <claire.liu@acme.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T18:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap + Next Steps: Context-length profiling & token-volume for pricing

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

Quick answers:
- Avg tokens today (approx): prompt 420 tokens (p50 ~ 300, p90 ~ 1,200), completion 1,050 tokens (p50 ~ 800, p90 ~ 2,500).
- Monthly volume: your estimate is close. Current production baseline: ~600M prompt tokens / 1.4B completion tokens (total ~2.0B tokens). Expect 2x growth in 6–9 months after pilot.
- Context-length needs: ~82% of requests fit within 8k, 15% need 32k, ~3% require 128k (mostly multi-doc summarization).
- Target budget: as a mid-market buyer we are targeting a unit economics goal of ~$80–$120 per 1M tokens (total tokens across prompt+completion) depending on SLA and model quality. Our immediate monthly budget for pilot evaluation is $8k–$15k.
- Model family: we prefer open models (Llama/Redwood-curated variants) but are open to a hybrid fallback to higher-SLA variants for critical paths.

Notes / asks:
- I populated the ContextLength_Profile_Template with a 100-request sample and attached it. The sample includes p50/p90 token metrics and flags for requests that pull >1 doc.
- Can you confirm how Redwood charges for context tokens vs. generated tokens when using caching (i.e., do cached prefixes reduce billable prompt tokens)? Also want to see a modeled $/1M under Balanced vs Cost-optimized options.

Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up if helpful.

Samir
Product Lead, Search & Assist | Acme Corp
samir@acme.com

---
Attachment: ContextLength_Profile_Template_filled.csv (csv, 12KB stub)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T01:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap + Next Steps: Context-length profiling & token-volume for pricing

On Tue, Apr 20, 2027 at 18:46, Samir Patel <samir@acme.com> wrote:
> (quoted above)

Thanks Samir — this is super helpful. A couple of quick technical clarifications so our cost model is accurate: 

1) When you say 3% require 128k, is that 3% of total requests but represent a much higher share of tokens? (we typically see 128k requests contribute 20–40% of token volume)
2) Do the 32k/128k requests include context that can be cached (repeated prefixes like customer profile + product info), or are they mostly unique per request?
3) Are there any throughput/latency SLOs for the summarization path (e.g., p95 < 1.5s or p95 < 5s acceptable)? Latency will materially change model and instance sizing for Dedicated.

If you can answer 1–3 we’ll send a modeled comparison (spreadsheet) showing: unit $/1M tokens for each model family, projected monthly spend at current volumes and at 2x growth, and the % savings from caching/quantization.

If helpful I can also propose a pilot config: 2 x A100s equivalent, 8k + 32k pools, autoscale policy for daytime bursts; that config is generally a good balance for mixed workloads.

—Jordan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com

From: Samir Patel <samir@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Liu <claire.liu@acme.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap + Next Steps: Context-length profiling & token-volume for pricing

Jordan / Marissa — quick follow-up:
1) Yes — the ~3% of 128k requests account for roughly 28% of our total token volume today (they are multi-doc summarizations with long customer histories).
2) About half of the 32k requests have cacheable prefixes (customer metadata + product index) — the 128k ones are mostly unique each time.
3) Latency: for interactive support assistant we need p95 < 2s; for async multi-doc batch summarization p95 < 10s is acceptable.

Given that, we’re very interested in the Balanced option you mentioned (lower latency, moderate cost). Please send the modeled spreadsheet and the two pricing options.

Samir
